title: Dress Code, Public Decorum, and Social Norms
summary: Egypt welcomes visitors with legendary hospitality (Karam) while expecting mutual respect for its deep-rooted social values, modest traditions, and sacred religious sites.

sections.heading: Dress Code Guidelines
content: General Public & Urban Areas: Modesty is respected across Egypt. In traditional neighborhoods, urban city centers, and historical quarters, wearing modest attire (covering shoulders and knees) reflects respect for local customs.
Resort Destinations: Red Sea coastal resorts (Sharm El Sheikh, Hurghada, El Gouna) follow international beach standards. Swimwear is entirely customary on private beaches and pool premises.

Religious Sites (Mosques & Churches): Modest clothing is mandatory. Women must cover their heads (scarf/hijab), shoulders, and legs when entering active mosques. Shoes must be removed prior to stepping onto prayer carpets.

sections.heading: Public Expressions of Affection (PDA) & Conduct
content: Public Affection Limits: Holding hands is universally acceptable. Excessive public displays of affection (passionate kissing, intimate physical contact) in public streets or family areas are socially inappropriate and may lead to complaints regarding public indecency under the Penal Code.
Public Order & Mutual Respect: Respecting public order, avoiding loud arguments, and honoring Egyptian hospitality form the foundation of positive community interactions.
